title: A Border for the Cover
premise: Rafael Villalobos, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group—a diplomatic front that exists on no ledger—has spent a decade perfecting his own erasure. When Flight 447's records evaporate mid-flight, he realizes someone inside the Group is burning their own history, and the defector he must extract, Dr. Ilse Brandt, is carrying an inheritance: her father's proof of who built the Group and why. As Rafael smuggles her across three borders, he discovers she knew his mother, a courier who vanished in 1989, and that the flight manifest was doctored to lure him out. In the end, Rafael chooses love and truth over duty, exposing the Group's founder—his own handler—and walking away with Ilse, leaving his polished lie behind for good.
about_author: Coral Lockridge is the pen name of a former foreign-service translator who spent years in postings she still cannot name. She writes thrillers about people whose passports are thinner than their secrets.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A routine night in Vienna: he burns a contact's identity, checks his go-bag, and rehearses his cover story over cheap wine. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness—the discipline of a man who has made himself untraceable, and the quiet dread that no one would notice if he disappeared.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He watches a Group asset's flight land—or not land; every record of it vanishes while it's airborne, radar logs included. His handler, Marek, orders him to treat it as a glitch. The beat is vertigo: for the first time, Rafael's own paper trail feels like it could dissolve beneath him.

chapters.title: The Defector's Price
chapters.summary: Ilse Brandt's POV. Waiting in a Trieste safehouse, Ilse reviews her father's documents one last time before handing them to strangers. She recognizes a name from her childhood—Rafael's mother. The beat is resolve sharpened by grief: she knows she may be bait, and comes anyway.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The Trieste pickup goes wrong in a precise way—too precise—suggesting someone sold the route. Rafael gets Ilse out through the fish market as shooters close in. The beat is adrenaline laced with suspicion: the ambush was designed to fail just enough to keep him running.

chapters.title: Borders Like Wounds
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A night drive toward Slovenia while Ilse explains what her father proved: the Group was founded to bury a Cold War atrocity, and its founders are still alive, still powerful. Rafael recognizes his mother's handwriting in the margins. The beat is reluctant intimacy between two people made of secrets.

chapters.title: What Marek Knew
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. In Vienna, Marek reports to the Group's unseen founder that the trap is sprung—but hesitates over one file: Rafael's mother's death record, which he falsified decades ago. The beat is guilt curdling into self-preservation; Marek realizes he may be next on the burn list.

chapters.title: The Safehouse That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Their fallback safehouse in Ljubljana is already compromised—someone used Rafael's own protocols to find it. Only three people know them. The beat is betrayal closing in like weather, and Rafael's cold clarity: the leak isn't sloppy, it's personal.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Holed up in a mountain chapel, Ilse shows Rafael the final document: his mother didn't defect—she was executed carrying the same proof, and Marek signed the order under duress. The beat is devastating recognition; Rafael's whole identity was built on a lie the Group authored.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owns the Silence
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Climax. Rafael walks into the Vienna office wearing his polished lie like armor, confronts the founder—an aging diplomat he's met a dozen times as 'Uncle Anton'—and trades the documents' release for Ilse's clean exit, recording everything. The beat is a man finally choosing which side of history to stand on.

chapters.title: A Border for the Cover
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Weeks later, at a quiet Adriatic crossing, two travelers with new names wait in line like anyone else. The files have gone to three newspapers; Marek testified and vanished. Rafael holds her hand as the border guard barely glances up. The beat is peace earned the hard way: visible at last, and free.
